title: Accuracy vs Precision
stem:
Two laboratory pH meters are compared. Meter 1 gives the true pH correctly in 85 out of 100 tests. Meter 2 gives the true pH correctly in 92 out of 100 tests. When each meter is used to re-test the same sample 50 times, Meter 1 returns the same reading 49 times and Meter 2 returns the same reading 42 times.

Which statement best compares the two meters?
answer_reason: Accuracy = how often the reading is correct. Meter 1 = 85%, Meter 2 = 92% — Meter 2 is more accurate. Precision = how consistent repeated readings are. Meter 1 = 49/50 = 98%, Meter 2 = 42/50 = 84% — Meter 1 is more precise. So Meter 2 is more accurate but Meter 1 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 1 is more accurate but Meter 2 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 2 is more accurate but Meter 1 is more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 2 is both more accurate and more precise.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Meter 1 is both more accurate and more precise.

title: Detentions Average
stem:
In a class of ten pupils, the average number of detentions per pupil this term is 3.6. Four pupils received three detentions each, three pupils received two detentions each, and one pupil received one detention. Of the remaining two pupils, Aisha received three more detentions than Ben.

How many detentions did Ben receive?
answer_reason: Total detentions = 10 × 3.6 = 36. Known detentions = (4 × 3) + (3 × 2) + 1 = 12 + 6 + 1 = 19. Aisha and Ben share 36 − 19 = 17 detentions. Aisha = Ben + 3, so Ben + (Ben + 3) = 17 ⇒ 2 × Ben = 14 ⇒ Ben = 7.

title: Conference Seating
stem:
Six delegates sit in a row of six chairs numbered 1 to 6 (left to right). Farah sits in chair 3. George sits immediately to the right of Farah. Hana sits in chair 1 or chair 6. Iqbal sits somewhere to the left of George but not in the chair directly next to Farah. Jasper and Kim take the remaining chairs. Kim does not sit directly next to Hana.

Which of the following seating arrangements, listed from chair 1 to chair 6, is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Farah = chair 3 and George = chair 4. Iqbal is left of George but not directly next to Farah, so Iqbal = chair 1 (chair 2 would be next to Farah). Hana is in chair 1 or 6; chair 1 is taken, so Hana = chair 6. Jasper and Kim take chairs 2 and 5. Kim cannot be directly next to Hana (chair 6), so Kim ≠ chair 5, meaning Kim = 2 and Jasper = 5. Order: Iqbal, Kim, Farah, George, Jasper, Hana — option B.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Iqbal, Jasper, Farah, George, Kim, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Iqbal, Kim, Farah, George, Jasper, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Jasper, Iqbal, Farah, George, Kim, Hana

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Hana, Iqbal, Farah, George, Jasper, Kim

title: Gym Class Attendance
stem: The table shows the number of attendees at four fitness classes over three months at a community gym.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Spin had the highest total attendance over the three months.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Spin totals 120 + 118 + 126 = 364. Yoga totals 286, Pilates 197, HIIT 173. Spin is the highest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every class saw attendance rise between February and March.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Yoga 92→110, Spin 118→126, Pilates 65→72, HIIT 58→70. Every class grew from February to March.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: HIIT will attract more attendees than Yoga in April.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The data does not extend to April. Extrapolating future trends from past data is not supported.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Pilates attendance grew by more than 20 percent from January to March.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Pilates went from 60 to 72 — an increase of 12. 12 / 60 = 0.20, so the growth is exactly 20%, not more than 20%.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Spin attendance dropped between January and February.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Spin went from 120 in January to 118 in February — a drop of 2.

title: Airport Passenger Profile
stem:
The diagram categorises passengers passing through an airport terminal on a weekend. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a weekend arrival who is a frequent flyer with checked baggage but is not a minor travelling alone?
answer_reason: Weekend arrival is the outer category; every labelled passenger sits inside it. The question asks for a passenger inside weekend arrival, checked baggage, and frequent flyer, but outside minor alone. Letter P is inside weekend arrival only. Letter Q is inside weekend arrival and checked baggage but not frequent flyer. Letter R is inside weekend arrival and frequent flyer but not checked baggage. Letter T is inside weekend arrival and minor alone — includes minor alone, which is excluded. Letter S is inside weekend arrival, checked baggage, and frequent flyer, and outside minor alone — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Coloured Marbles
stem:
A bag contains 5 red marbles, 4 blue marbles and 3 green marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement.

What is the probability that both marbles are blue?
answer_reason: Total marbles = 12. P(first blue) = 4/12 = 1/3. After one blue is removed, 3 blues remain in 11 marbles. P(second blue | first blue) = 3/11. P(both blue) = (1/3) × (3/11) = 3/33 = 1/11.

title: Morning Shift Deliveries
stem:
A courier logs 90 deliveries one day. 42 are classed as priority, 35 are oversized, 30 fall within the morning shift window.

14 deliveries are both priority and oversized. 12 priority deliveries fall within the morning shift window. 10 oversized deliveries fall within the morning shift window. 6 deliveries are all three. 17 deliveries are none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 6 deliveries are in all three and 17 are outside. Scan — A shows 4 in the centre — eliminate A. B shows 22 outside — eliminate B. That leaves C and D. The stem says 14 are priority and oversized, and 6 of those are also morning shift, so priority-and-oversized only = 14 − 6 = 8. C shows 8 ✓. D shows 12 — eliminate D. Answer: C.

title: Exam Pipeline
stem:
The diagram shows candidates progressing through five stages of an exam pipeline: registered, screening, written test, oral test, and practical. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a candidate who reached the written test and the oral test, but not the practical and not any earlier stage?
answer_reason: Consecutive stages overlap in the diagram; non-consecutive stages do not. The question asks for the region inside the written test and the oral test but outside the practical and outside every earlier stage. Letter P is registered only. Letter Q is registered and at screening. Letter R is at screening and the written test — not the oral test. Letter S is at the written test and the oral test, and outside every other stage — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Commute Pipeline
stem:
160 commuters were surveyed on three legs of their morning commute: local train, tube, and office bus. No one takes the tube without also taking the local train, and no one takes the office bus without also taking the tube.

48 commuters took the local train only. 24 took both the local train and the tube but not the office bus. 18 took both the tube and the office bus. 52 took none of the three legs.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 52 took none of the three and 18 took office bus + tube + local train. Scan — B shows 45 outside — eliminate B. D shows 12 in the triple overlap — eliminate D. That leaves A and C. The stem says 18 took tube and office bus; all of those also took the local train (per the consecutive-legs rule) — so tube-and-office-bus-only = 18 − 18 = 0, and that region should be omitted. A has no tube-and-office-bus-only region ✓. C has a tube-and-office-bus-only region of 6, which would mean 6 commuters took the office bus without the local train — violates the consecutive rule. Eliminate C. Answer: A.

title: Bookshop Orders
stem:
An online bookshop processes 140 orders one week across three categories: gift-wrapped, dispatched by first-class post, and placed by members.

38 orders are gift-wrapped, 52 are dispatched by first-class post, and 60 are placed by members. 12 orders are both gift-wrapped and dispatched by first-class post. 22 orders are both dispatched by first-class post and placed by members. 14 orders are both gift-wrapped and placed by members. 6 orders fall into all three categories. 14 orders are none of the three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 6 orders are in all three categories and 14 are outside. Scan — C shows 10 in the centre — eliminate C. D shows 20 outside — eliminate D. That leaves A and B. The stem says 12 orders are gift-wrapped and dispatched by first-class post; 6 of those are also members, so gift-wrapped-and-first-class only = 12 − 6 = 6. A shows 6 ✓. B shows 10 — eliminate B. Answer: A.

title: Rare Disease Test
stem:
A rare disease affects 1 in 2,000 adults. A screening test is 98% sensitive (correctly identifies 98% of people who have the disease) and 95% specific (correctly identifies 95% of people who do not have the disease).

If an adult from this population tests positive, roughly what is the probability they actually have the disease?
answer_reason: Imagine 100,000 adults: 50 have the disease, 99,950 do not. True positives ≈ 98% × 50 = 49. False positives = 5% × 99,950 ≈ 4,998. Total positives ≈ 5,047. P(disease | positive) ≈ 49 / 5,047 ≈ 1%. The high test accuracy does not overcome the very low base rate.

title: Hobby Club Membership
stem:
The diagram shows members of a hobby club categorised by five activities: chess, baking, hiking, pottery, and drama. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a member who takes part in baking and hiking but neither chess, pottery, nor drama?
answer_reason: Consecutive activities overlap in the diagram; non-consecutive activities do not, because no one takes a later activity without taking every earlier one. The question asks for the region inside baking and hiking but outside chess, pottery, and drama. Letter P sits inside chess only. Letter Q sits inside chess and baking — includes chess, which is excluded. Letter S sits inside hiking and pottery — includes pottery, which is excluded. Letter R sits inside baking and hiking, outside chess, pottery, and drama — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter R.

title: Later School Start
stem: Should secondary schools in the UK move the start of the school day from 08:45 to 10:00 to improve student academic performance?
answer_reason: B connects the action (later start) to the outcome (academic performance) with study evidence. A addresses preference, not performance. C addresses logistics, not performance. D assumes teaching quality is the only relevant factor and doesn't address whether a later start could still help.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; teenagers tend to get up late at the weekend, so they would prefer a later start.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; multiple controlled studies have shown that moving start times to after 09:30 increases average exam scores by around 4% in secondary-age students, directly improving academic performance.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; parents of younger children would need to rearrange school runs, causing logistical problems.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; academic performance depends on teaching quality, which a later start will not change.

title: Only Pilots
stem: Only qualified pilots may land at the private airstrip. Every qualified pilot has passed the medical review. Some people who have passed the medical review are instructors. No instructor uses the short runway.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Anyone who lands at the private airstrip has passed the medical review.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only qualified pilots may land there, and all qualified pilots have passed the medical review — so anyone landing has passed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All instructors are qualified pilots.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say some people who passed the medical are instructors, not that all instructors are pilots. Instructors might not be pilots at all.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some qualified pilots are instructors.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know some medical-reviewed people are instructors, but those instructors are not guaranteed to be pilots — being a pilot is a stricter category.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No instructor may land at the private airstrip.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some instructors could also be qualified pilots — the premises do not forbid it, so we cannot rule out instructors landing.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every person who uses the short runway is not an instructor.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No instructor uses the short runway, so everyone using it must be a non-instructor.

title: Team Pairing
stem:
A manager must pair four new hires (Priya, Quinn, Ravi, Sam) with four mentors (Wren, Xia, Yousef, Zane) for a six-month programme. Each mentor takes exactly one new hire. Wren mentors Sam. Xia will only mentor Ravi. Yousef refuses to mentor Quinn.

Which of the following pairings of new hires with mentors is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Wren mentors Sam and Xia mentors Ravi. That leaves Yousef and Zane to pair with Priya and Quinn. Yousef refuses Quinn, so Yousef = Priya and Zane = Quinn. Final pairing: Priya-Yousef, Quinn-Zane, Ravi-Xia, Sam-Wren — option A. Option B swaps Yousef and Zane, breaking the Yousef/Quinn constraint. Option C places Priya with Xia (only Ravi allowed). Option D puts Quinn with Wren and Sam with Zane, breaking Wren=Sam.

title: Cycle Helmet Law
stem: Should it be made compulsory for all adult cyclists to wear helmets to reduce head injuries on UK roads?
answer_reason: A directly links the action (mandatory helmets) to the outcome (reduced head injuries) with specific evidence. B addresses practicality but not head injuries. C is opinion-based and narrow. D addresses a tangential outcome (physical activity) rather than head injuries. A is the strongest.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a 2022 review of UK hospital data found cyclists wearing helmets had 45% fewer serious head injuries than those without, so a legal requirement would directly reduce head injuries.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; helmets are inexpensive and most cyclists already carry one.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; some cyclists find helmets uncomfortable on long rides.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; mandatory helmet laws discourage some people from cycling, which reduces physical activity across the population.

title: Lab Access
stem: A key card cannot unlock the laboratory unless it has been registered this month. Every key card registered this month shows a green indicator light. Only senior staff may register more than one key card. No visitor is senior staff.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every key card that can unlock the laboratory shows a green indicator light.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: A card can only unlock the lab if it has been registered this month, and every registered card shows a green indicator. So any unlocking card must show green.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a key card shows a green indicator light, it must have been registered this month.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise is one-way: registered → green. Other cards could also display green for unrelated reasons, so green does not guarantee registration.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No visitor may register more than one key card.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Only senior staff may register more than one card, and no visitor is senior staff, so no visitor has that privilege.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every visitor has been issued a key card that unlocks the laboratory.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premises say nothing about whether visitors are issued unlocking cards. Unmentioned = No.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a key card has not been registered this month, it cannot unlock the laboratory.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: This is the contrapositive of the "unless" rule: unlocking requires registration, so failing to register means the card cannot unlock the lab.

title: Remote Working Study
stem: A management consultancy reports that teams who adopted fully remote working in 2023 saw a 12% rise in self-reported productivity. Critics note the same teams also reported higher rates of burnout and that the productivity measure relied on self-assessment rather than objective output metrics. The consultancy acknowledges these limitations but argues the results still support remote working.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Remote working caused a 12% rise in productivity for the teams studied.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage reports a rise coinciding with remote working — not a proven causal link. Correlation is not causation.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The productivity measure in the study was based on self-assessment.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage explicitly states the productivity measure relied on self-assessment rather than objective output metrics.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The teams studied reported higher burnout after adopting remote working.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated by the critics cited in the passage.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The consultancy considers remote working unsuitable for all teams.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The consultancy still argues the results support remote working, not that it is unsuitable for all teams.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Objective productivity data would show the same 12% rise.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No objective data is reported; the passage says the measure was self-assessment. We cannot predict what objective data would show.

title: UK Export Orders
stem:
A manufacturer ships 100 orders. 45 are exported, 40 are bulk orders, 55 are dispatched from within the UK region.

Among exported orders, 20 are also bulk. Among bulk orders, 25 are dispatched from within the UK region. Among exported orders, 22 are dispatched from within the UK region. 12 orders fall into all three categories. 18 orders are none of these three.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Freebies: 12 orders are in all three categories and 18 are outside. Scan — A shows 15 in the centre — eliminate A. D shows 25 outside — eliminate D. That leaves B and C. The stem says 20 are exported and bulk, and 12 of those are also inside UK, so exported-and-bulk only = 20 − 12 = 8. B shows 8 ✓. C shows 10 — eliminate C. Answer: B.

title: Independent Alarms
stem:
A warehouse has two independent smoke alarms. Alarm X correctly triggers in 90% of fires. Alarm Y correctly triggers in 80% of fires.

What is the probability that at least one alarm triggers in the event of a fire?
answer_reason: P(neither triggers) = P(X fails) × P(Y fails) = 0.10 × 0.20 = 0.02. P(at least one triggers) = 1 − 0.02 = 0.98 = 98%.

title: Sterile Kits
stem: A surgical kit is safe to use if and only if it has been sterilised and sealed. All sealed kits carry a blue tag. Sterilisation is necessary for a kit to be reused. Some kits without blue tags have been opened.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every safe-to-use kit carries a blue tag.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Safe to use requires sealing, and every sealed kit carries a blue tag — therefore every safe kit carries a blue tag.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A kit without a blue tag cannot be reused.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reuse requires sterilisation, not sealing. A kit could be sterilised but not sealed — so it might lack a blue tag yet still meet the reuse condition.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some opened kits have not been sealed.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some kits without blue tags have been opened. Every sealed kit has a blue tag, so a no-blue-tag kit is not sealed. These opened, no-tag kits are therefore unsealed.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: If a kit has been sterilised, it is safe to use.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Safe to use requires BOTH sterilisation AND sealing. Sterilisation alone is not enough.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every safe-to-use kit can be reused.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Sterilisation is a necessary condition for reuse, not a sufficient one. A safe kit meets the sterilisation requirement but may fail other reuse requirements the premises do not list.

title: Sugar Tax on Snacks
stem: Should the government extend the sugar tax from soft drinks to all packaged snack foods to reduce childhood obesity?
answer_reason: B links the action (tax on snacks) to the outcome (childhood obesity) with specific evidence and NHS modelling. A assumes transfer between categories without evidence. C addresses tax revenue, not obesity. D makes a sweeping assumption that contradicts established evidence and ignores diet as a factor.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; households with young children already buy fewer sugary soft drinks since the 2018 tax, so extending it will make them buy fewer snacks too.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; data from the UK soft drink levy shows a 10% reduction in sugar consumption among children since 2018, and NHS modelling predicts a similar tax on snacks would cut childhood obesity rates by 5–7% over ten years.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; food manufacturers would simply reformulate products to avoid the tax, so the tax would collect little revenue.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; childhood obesity is caused by low physical activity, not by diet.

title: Import Warehouse
stem:
A warehouse receives 120 consignments in a month. 55 are imported, 48 are perishable, and 40 require cold storage. 18 are imported and perishable, 14 are imported and requiring cold storage, and 22 are perishable and requiring cold storage. 8 fall into all three categories. 35 do not fall into any of these three categories.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
answer_reason: Two freebies: 8 consignments are in all three categories and 35 fall outside all three. Scan — C shows 12 in the centre, stem says 8 — eliminate C. D shows 40 outside, stem says 35 — eliminate D. That leaves A and B. The stem says 18 are imported and perishable, 8 of those are also cold storage, so imported-and-perishable only = 18 − 8 = 10. A shows 10 ✓. B shows 14 — eliminate B. Answer: A.

title: Delivery Vehicles
stem: A courier company runs 80 vehicles. 50 are vans and the rest are motorbikes. Every motorbike is electric. None of the red vehicles are motorbikes. Half of the vans are white.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Every red vehicle is a van.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The fleet is vans or motorbikes. No motorbike is red, so any red vehicle must be a van.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some motorbikes are red.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says none of the red vehicles are motorbikes — so no motorbike is red.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All electric vehicles in the fleet are motorbikes.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Every motorbike is electric, but vans could also be electric — we have no information ruling that out.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are exactly 25 white vans in the fleet.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Half of the 50 vans are white, which is 25 vans.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: There are more white vehicles than red vehicles in the fleet.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know 25 vans are white, but we do not know the number of red vehicles (only that none are motorbikes). The comparison cannot be made.

title: Regional Rainfall
stem: The table shows average monthly rainfall (mm) in four UK regions over four months in 2024.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Scotland had the highest rainfall in every month shown.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Scotland 110 > NW 92, SE 52, Mid 65 in April; Scotland 95 > others in May; Scotland 84 > others in June; Scotland 70 > others in July.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Rainfall fell in every region between April and July.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: NW 92→58, SE 52→38, Mid 65→48, Scotland 110→70. Every region saw rainfall fall.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The South East had less than half the rainfall of Scotland in April.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Half of 110 is 55. The South East had 52, which is less than 55.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The Midlands typically has a drier climate than the South East.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The table shows the opposite — Midlands rainfall exceeds South East rainfall in every month shown. "Typically" also extrapolates beyond the four months of data.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The North West recorded exactly 292 mm of rainfall across the four months.

title: Bloons and Grems
stem: All bloons are grems. Some grems are sprocks. No sprocks are doofs. Most doofs are nims.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some bloons are sprocks.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Bloons are grems, and only some grems are sprocks. The bloons could all fall among the non-sprock grems, so we cannot guarantee any bloon is a sprock.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some grems are not doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some grems are sprocks, and no sprocks are doofs. So those sprock-grems are not doofs — at least some grems are not doofs.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No bloons are doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know nothing about whether bloons are doofs. Bloons are grems, but grems are not restricted from being doofs.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Most nims are doofs.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Reverse inference. "Most doofs are nims" does not mean most nims are doofs — the nim population could be much larger.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All bloons are grems.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Directly stated in the premises.

title: Booking Order
stem:
Five consecutive appointments on Monday morning were booked by Aisha, Ben, Chloe, Dan, and Ellie (not necessarily in that order). Dan was booked immediately before Ellie. Aisha was booked before Ben, with at least one other person between them. Chloe was not the first or last appointment. Ben was not the last appointment.

Which of the following lists the appointments in order, from first to last, in a way that is consistent with all the constraints?
answer_reason: Dan is immediately before Ellie, so Dan-Ellie occupy consecutive positions. Ben is not last, so Ellie must be last — placing Dan-Ellie at positions 4-5. That leaves positions 1, 2, 3 for Aisha, Ben, Chloe. Chloe cannot be first or last, so Chloe is in position 2. Aisha is before Ben with at least one person between them, so Aisha = 1 and Ben = 3 (with Chloe between them). Order: Aisha, Chloe, Ben, Dan, Ellie — option A.

title: Plastic Cutlery Ban
stem: Should single-use plastic cutlery be banned nationwide to reduce marine plastic pollution?
answer_reason: A connects the action (ban) to the outcome (marine pollution) with evidence that cutlery is a significant source. B addresses preference, not pollution. C addresses business cost, not pollution. D deflects by comparing sources but does not address whether banning cutlery would still reduce pollution.

decision_making_question_options.label: A
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; a recent beach survey found plastic cutlery in the top five items recovered from UK coastlines, and a national ban would remove this source of marine litter.

decision_making_question_options.label: B
decision_making_question_options.option_text: Yes; plastic cutlery is unpleasant to use compared with wooden alternatives.

decision_making_question_options.label: C
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; many small takeaways rely on plastic cutlery and would find replacements expensive.

decision_making_question_options.label: D
decision_making_question_options.option_text: No; most marine plastic pollution comes from fishing gear, not cutlery.

title: Workforce Profile
stem:
The diagram categorises a company's workforce by employment attributes. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a part-time remote worker who is neither a graduate trainee nor a contractor?
answer_reason: The question asks for a person inside workforce, remote worker, and part-time, but outside graduate trainee and contractor. Letter P is only in the workforce, no attribute. Letter Q is in the workforce and remote worker but not part-time. Letter R is in the workforce, remote worker, and graduate trainee — includes graduate trainee, which is excluded. Letter S is in the workforce, remote worker, and part-time, and outside graduate trainee and contractor — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter S.

title: Staff Benefits Portal
stem:
The diagram shows how company staff are registered for the staff benefits portal. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents a staff member who is registered on the portal and takes up the travel pass benefit but no other benefit?
answer_reason: The question asks for staff inside registered AND travel pass, and outside every other benefit. Letter P is registered only, no benefit. Letter Q is registered and cycle-to-work, not travel pass. Letter R is registered and on the dental plan, not travel pass. Letter U is inside registered and travel pass, and outside every other benefit — that is the region we want. Answer: Letter U.
